source: Sifrei Bamidbar 1:3; Sifrei Bamidbar 1:4; Sifrei Bamidbar 1:7; Onkelos Num 5:2; Onkelos Num 5:3
claim_en: THREE CAMP-WORDS, THREE CAMPS. The command writes 'the camp' (5:2), 'outside the camp' and 'their camps' (5:3) — three (computed on the ink) — and the Sifrei derives from the threefold word the THREE CAMPS: Israel's, the Levites', the Shekhinah's (mapped onto Jerusalem: to the Temple mount, to the courtyard, inward), with the ladder of stringency that sends the leper from three, the man with a discharge from two, the corpse-unclean from one (rows 1:4, 1:7); Onkelos 'every one shut up, every one who flows, every one unclean by a man's corpse' names the three by their signs. The exam: Mishnah Kelim 1:5-9; Zevachim 116b; Pesachim 67a.
middah: plain (the Sifrei's derivation from the counted repetition; the three camp-words computed on the ink)

source: Sifrei Bamidbar 1:1; Sifrei Bamidbar 1:2; Onkelos Num 5:2; Onkelos Num 5:3; Onkelos Num 5:4
claim_en: THE WARNING FOR THE PUNISHMENT; 'COMMAND' FOUR WAYS. The Sifrei opens: Num 19:20 gives the PUNISHMENT for defiling the sanctuary (excision) and no warning — 5:2-3's 'send out... they shall not defile their camps' IS the warning: the punishment/warning pairing the courts require, seated on this clause (row 1:1); and 'command' read four ways — immediate and for the generations (from the run at 5:4 and Lev 24:2-3), impulsion (R. Yehudah b. Beteira), expense (R. Shimon b. Yochai), exhortation (Rebbi) — a dispute on the lemma, four settings recorded (row 1:2); the run 5:4 doubled ('so' twice, 'the children of Israel' twice — computed): the unclean did not protest (row 1:8).
middah: plain (the warning identified by the Sifrei's own pairing; the four readings of the lemma recorded as a dispute)

claim_en: MY SHEKHINAH IN THEIR MIDST. 'In whose midst I dwell' (5:3 — with 35:34 the Torah's two seats of the clause, computed) → Onkelos 'in whose midst MY SHEKHINAH dwells' — the first person rendered by the Presence-word; the Sifrei's row on the same words: 'beloved are Israel — even when unclean, the Shekhinah is among them' (Lev 16:16; Num 35:34) — the translation's noun and the Sifrei's are one.
middah: plain (the rendering read as it stands beside the Sifrei's statement; the clause's seats computed)

check.note: '[I] dwell' — the clause the Aramaic renders by the Shekhinah

claim_en: ME'ILAH IS LYING — THE SPINE AGREES WITH ITSELF, AND THE NOUN IS TOLD BY ITS POINTS. 'To commit a trespass against the LORD' → Onkelos 'TO LIE A LIE before the LORD' (again at 5:12 and 5:27); the Sifrei's rule on the same verse, 'me'ilah in all places is lying', with five proof-seats (1 Chr 5:25, Josh 7:1, 1 Chr 10:13, 2 Chr 26:18, Num 5:12); and THE NOUN BY ITS POINTS: the trespass-word with a patach (the short a-vowel) under both letters at 13 Tanakh seats (Lev 5:15, 5:21, Num 5:6, 5:27, 31:16, Josh 7:1 among them) against 'from upon' with a tsere (the long e-vowel) at 191 — the same consonants, two words (computed on the DB's code points; sitting 1b's law at a third word).
middah: ink (the homograph split by the points on the DB; the two members of the spine read as they stand)

check.note: 'a trespass' — the noun with the patach

source: Sifrei Bamidbar 2:1; Sifrei Bamidbar 4:1; Sifrei Bamidbar 4:2; Sifrei Bamidbar 4:3; Sifrei Bamidbar 4:4; Onkelos Num 5:7; Onkelos Num 5:8
claim_en: THE RULE OF REPETITION: THE PROSELYTE'S THEFT GOES TO THE WATCH, THE MONEY BEFORE THE RAM. Why the section, already at Lev 5:20-26? 'Any section stated in one place, missing one thing, and repeated elsewhere is repeated only for the thing originated' (the middot's own case law — the Sifrei on 5:6): the dead proselyte without an heir — 'if the man has no redeemer' (R. Yishmael: who in Israel has none? the proselyte); the principal and the fifth to the OFFICIATING WATCH ('whereby atonement is made for him'), the ram to the altar; the priest-thief does not keep it (the a-fortiori refuted by a distinction); the proselyte dies first — the heirs exempt from the ram, and after the money is given it stays (R. Akiva after Zifron); the money must precede the ram, two watches or one (rows 4:1-4). Onkelos 'redeemer' (the kinsman-word), 'the ram of atonements'. The exam: Mishnah Bava Kamma 9:11-12; Bava Kamma 109a-111a.
middah: plain (the Sifrei's meta-rule and its rows read as they stand; the a-fortiori of row 4:2 refuted by the source itself)

claim_en: THE FIFTH — ITS BASE DISPUTED; HIS OWN SIN; THE THING ITSELF. 'And its fifth he shall add to it' (the fifth-clause's Torah seats Lev 5:16, 5:24, 27:13, Num 5:7 — computed): R. Yoshiyah — a fifth of the WHOLE (it and its fifth make five equal parts: a quarter of the principal); R. Yonathan — a fifth of the principal — a dispute on the base, both recorded (the exam's Bava Metzia 54a); 'their sin which they did' — not the father's; 'restore at its head' — the stolen thing itself may be returned; 'to whom he is liable' — the court's messenger or the heir; Onkelos 'return his debt at its head'.
middah: plain (the dispute recorded as a dispute; the clauses read as they stand)

source: Onkelos Num 5:9; Onkelos Num 5:10; Sifrei Bamidbar 5:1; Sifrei Bamidbar 6:1; Sifrei Bamidbar 6:2
claim_en: THE TITHE INSERTED; THE FIRST FRUITS' RECIPIENT; THE FIRSTBORN'S THIRTY DAYS. 'A man's holy things shall be his' (5:10, one seat) → Onkelos 'THE TITHE of his holy things shall be his' — a word the Hebrew lacks, cut from the shelf's bytes: the translation names which holy thing stays the owner's, one of the Sifrei's list (the thank and peace portions, the paschal lamb, the animal tithe, the second tithe, the fourth-year fruit — row 6:1, with the fourth-year dispute); 'which they bring near to the priest' (5:9) — not terumah, which the priest fetches, but the FIRST FRUITS, whose recipient Exod 23:19 left unnamed (row 5:1); and R. Yossi on 5:10: a son redeemed within thirty days who dies — the money returns; after thirty — it stays (row 6:2): the firstborn engine's thirty-day row at a Naso seat (Bekhorot 49a).
middah: plain (the inserted word cut from the shelf; the Sifrei's rows read as they stand; the thirty-day rule a standing cell)

check.note: 'his holy things' — the clause Onkelos narrows to the tithe
